What to look for in summer gloves

  • Knuckle and palm protection. Look for hard or moulded knuckle armour and palm sliders that resist abrasion.
  • Waterproofing. A membrane like Gore-Tex or Drystar keeps hands dry — vital for safe control in UK rain.
  • Fit and feel. Gloves should be snug with no loose fingertips so you keep full control of the levers.
  • Season-specific. Vented summer gloves and insulated winter gloves do very different jobs — many tourers own both.

Frequently asked questions

How much should I spend on summer gloves?

Our catalogue spans £34.75 to £190. Budget options under £150 cover the essentials, the £150–£400 mid-range hits the sweet spot for most UK tourers, and premium picks above £400 add refinement, lighter materials and longer-term durability.

Which brands are worth considering?

Popular, well-reviewed brands in this category include Klim, Rev'it, Alpinestars, Spidi, RST. All are stocked by SportsBikeShop with UK warranty support.

Do I really need waterproof kit?

In the UK, yes. Cold, wet hands and feet impair control and concentration within minutes. A waterproof membrane is one of the best touring upgrades you can make.

faq.q: Are perforated summer gloves safe in a crash?
faq.a: Perforated leather gloves like the Klim Badlands Aero Pro still offer strong abrasion resistance plus hard knuckle armour, so they are a sound choice. Full mesh textile gloves such as the RST S1 Mesh are cooler but give up some protection, so weigh comfort against risk.

Perforated leather balances airflow and protection and lasts longer, but costs more. Air-mesh textile gloves are cheapest and coolest, ideal for slow town riding. If you ride quickly or tour, lean towards perforated leather like the Klim or Rev'it Speedart Air.

faq.q: Will summer gloves cope with a shower?
faq.a: No. Vented gloves are designed to flow air, so they soak through quickly and take a while to dry. On changeable UK days carry a compact waterproof pair, or choose a membrane glove if rain is likely on your route.

faq.q: Should I size summer gloves tightly?
faq.a: A snug, close fit gives the best feel and stops fingertips bunching, and thin summer gloves have little lining to break in. Leave just enough room to flex your fingers freely, but avoid loose material that reduces control at the levers.
